newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEVI, JOHNSON SHARE HARTFORD OPEN LEAD, DALY RETURNS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEVI, JOHNSON SHARE HARTFORD OPEN LEAD, DALY RETURNS.

text.p: Former champion Wayne Levi, who has fallen on lean times, and unheralded rookie Eric Johnson both fired six-under-par rounds of 64 on Thursday to share the first-round lead at the Greater Hartford Open.
Levi, who won here in 1990, did not make a bogey, a distinction matched by Johnson, who has missed the cut in 10 of 16 events this year.

Steve Pate was alone in third place after a five-under 65. J.P. Hayes, Tom Byrum, Joe Durant and Doug Barron were two shots off the pace after 66s, with New England native Brad Faxon leading a group of 12 players at 67.

John Daly made his return to the PGA Tour after a five-week absence and posted a one-over 71. The former PGA and British Open champion was playing for the first time since withdrawing from last month's U.S. Open citing difficulties stemming from his alcoholism treatment.

Johnson climbed up the leaderboard by stringing together birdie putts at the 11th, 12th and 13th holes. Playing in one of the last groups, he gained a share of the lead with a six-foot birdie at the par-3 16th hole.

"I didn't mis-hit too many shots today, plus I had some good up-and-downs," observed Johnson, who qualified for the Tour by finishing 10th on the 1996 Nike Tour money list. "It was the most solid ball-striking round I've had."
Johnson also has played on the Asian Tour, Jordan Tour, Emerald Coast Tour, Hurricane Tour and Carolina Tour, once collecting checks on six different tours in one year.

Levi's self-described "solid round," started on the back nine with birdies at 11 and 12. He ended a run of seven consecutive pars with back-to-back birdies at the second and third holes, then birdied seven and nine.
"I never got in any trouble," said Levi. "When you don't make mistakes, you can score well."
Levy's victory here in 1990 was one of four triumphs he enjoyed in 1990 on his way to Player of the Year honours. He has not won a tournament since.
"I've been playing okay," Levy said. "I'm not working as hard on my game as I used to."
This week's field is relatively weak since many of the top players have taken time off following the British Open. Justin Leonard, the victor at Royal Troon, is among the missing, as is Tiger Woods.
First prize in the tournament is $270,000.
